- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is significantly above true price, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.
- If recent history shows sharp upward spikes followed by model overreaction (forecast > true), apply a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% per day after peak.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is consistently below true, adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect bullish sentiment bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, apply mean reversion: pull forecast toward 14-day MA by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative trend (e.g., 3 consecutive low sentiment values), reduce forecast slope by 15–20% to avoid “sentiment overfitting”.
- For forecasts with high volatility (true outcome variance > 3% per day), apply smoothing: reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to match observed stability.
